title: Regimental Histories
summary: --Regimental histories is a free-floating topical subdivision under names of wars for histories of individual participating military units below the level of a branch of the armed forces. It may be subdivided only by country (never smaller jurisdictions) and never by the name of the unit; the unit's corporate name is assigned as an additional heading. Works on a whole branch of the armed forces in a war take [country]. [Branch]--History--[war] instead.
validation_rules: `--Regimental histories` is a free-floating topical subdivision used under names of wars (including `[country]--History--[war]` forms), e.g. `United States--History--Civil War, 1861-1865--Regimental histories`, `World War, 1939-1945--Regimental histories--United States`. (H 1995 sec. 1, 4)
`--Regimental histories` applies to any organizational unit lower than a branch of the armed forces (divisions, regiments, fleets, squadrons, etc.). (H 1995 sec. 2)
`--Regimental histories` may be followed only by the name of the country to which the organization belongs; do not subdivide it by a jurisdiction smaller than a country. (H 1995 sec. 3)
Do not subdivide `--Regimental histories` or `--Regimental histories--[country]` by the name of the military unit. (H 1995 sec. 3)
Assign the corporate name of the military unit (e.g. `United States. Army. Armored Division, 3rd--History`) as an additional heading. (H 1995 sec. 4)

For U.S. wars established as period subdivisions under a state or locality, also assign `[name of state or locality]--History--[name of war]--Regimental histories` when appropriate (per H 1200 sec. 3.b). (H 1995 sec. 4)

For works on a whole branch of a country's armed forces during a war, use a heading of the type `United States. Army--History--World War, 1939-1945` (per H 1159), in addition to a heading for the war; do not then use `[war]--Regimental histories`. (H 1995 sec. 5)

sections.heading: 1. General rule
sections.text: Use the subdivision --Regimental histories as a free-floating topical subdivision under names of wars for histories of individual participating military organizations for the period of the war.

sections.heading: 2. Generic usage
sections.text: Use the subdivision in the generic sense for the history of any organizational unit lower than a branch of the armed forces, including individual divisions, regiments, fleets, squadrons, etc.

sections.heading: 3. Geographic subdivision
sections.text:
Further subdivide the subdivision, if appropriate, by the name of the country to which the organization belongs; do not subdivide --Regimental histories by a jurisdiction smaller than a country.

Do not further subdivide the subdivision --Regimental histories or the subdivision --Regimental histories--[country] by the name of the military unit.

sections.heading: 4. Usage under names of wars
sections.text:
When using the subdivision under names of wars, assign as an additional subject heading the corporate name of the individual military unit. Examples:

```
651 #0 $a United States $x History $y Civil War, 1861-1865 $x Regimental histories.
610 10 $a United States. $b Army. $b Pennsylvania Cavalry Regiment, 7th (1861-1865) $x History.

650 #0 $a World War, 1939-1945 $x Regimental histories $z United States.
610 10 $a United States. $b Army. $b Armored Division, 3rd $x History.
```

In accordance with H 1200, sec. 3.b., for wars established as subdivisions under the United States, also assign the heading [name of state or locality]--History--[name of war]--Regimental histories, if the war has been established as a period subdivision under the state or locality in question and if appropriate for the work being cataloged.

sections.heading: 5. Branch of the armed forces
sections.text:
For a work that deals specifically and exclusively with the activities of a particular branch of a country's armed forces during a war, assign a heading of the type United States. Army--History--World War, 1939-1945 in accordance with H 1159.

Headings of this type are assigned only in addition to a heading designating the particular war (with topical or local subdivisions, as appropriate). Do not assign in such cases a heading for the war with the subdivision --Regimental histories.
